units.title: 3.1 Unit: What is business? Managing marketing and finance

outcomes.text: Explain financial and non-financial reasons for setting up in business.
Describe entrepreneur characteristics: risk-taking, resilience, focus, passion, innovation, adaptability.
Explain the challenges of setting up and how the entrepreneur's role changes as the business grows.
Explain the purpose and value of a business plan and the importance of competitiveness.
Explain influences on decisions: objectives, risk, reward, resources, markets, ethics, opportunity cost.
Weigh risks and rewards and ethical dilemmas such as profit versus ethics.
Explain the purpose of objectives and what makes them SMART.
Describe sole traders, private and public limited companies, co-operatives and social enterprises.
Compare forms of business by control, objectives, finance, profit distribution and liability.
Explain why people buy shares and what moves share prices.
Calculate and interpret market capitalisation, dividends per share and dividend yield.
Distinguish internal stakeholders (employees, owners) from external ones (customers, suppliers, creditors, community, government).
Analyse the impact of business activity on stakeholders and ethical responsibilities to them.
Explain the purpose of market research, primary versus secondary, quantitative versus qualitative.
Interpret confidence levels and intervals and explain the value of market mapping.
Explain influences on how research is done: risk, cost, time, reliability.
Explain implications of B2B, B2C, C2C markets and goods versus services.
Explain effects of competition, competitive behaviour and market growth.
Calculate market size, market and sales growth, market share, sales data and return on marketing spend.
Interpret sales volume versus value and correlation; use index numbers and percentage changes.
Explain influences on demand.
Calculate and interpret price and income elasticity of demand.
Analyse the effect of price and income changes on revenue and quantity demanded.
Explain market segmentation: demographic, geographic, psychographic, behavioural.
Explain influences on choosing and entering a target market.
Compare niche and mass markets and adapt the marketing mix for a target market.
Explain marketing objectives: leads, sales, market share, brand awareness, retention, engagement, conversion.
Explain influences on marketing objectives and the budget.
Analyse how changes in demand (rise, fall, cyclical, seasonal) affect the marketing mix.
Explain links between marketing and other functions and its effect on competitiveness.
Explain the product life cycle stages and extension strategies.
Use the Boston Matrix for portfolio analysis.
Explain the purpose, value and challenges of new product development.
Explain influences on price and its impact on volume, revenue and margins.
Compare cost-based, demand-based (penetration, skimming, dynamic) and competition-based pricing.
Explain the purpose of a distribution channel.
Weigh direct distribution and e-commerce against using intermediaries.
Weigh different channels and multi-channel distribution.
Explain the purpose and value of promotion, advertising, social media and influencers, sales promotions, sponsorship and personal selling.
Explain the value of branding, brand loyalty and own-label brands, and influences on the promotional mix.
Explain the use of digital technology and AI in marketing: social media, content, SEO, PPC, cookies.
Measure digital marketing success: search performance, click-through, time on site, conversion, subscribers, ad revenue.
Explain CRM and data analytics in marketing and the effect on competitiveness.
Explain financial objectives: profit, profitability, cash flow, liquidity, borrowing.
Explain influences on financial objectives, links to other functions and effect on competitiveness.
Weigh internal sources: owners' investment, retained profit, asset sales, sale and leaseback, working capital.
Weigh external sources: trade credit, shares, overdraft, loans, business angels, private equity, crowd funding.
Judge the suitability of a source for a business.
Calculate fixed, variable and total costs, revenue, contribution, break-even output and margin of safety.
Interpret break-even charts and show effects of price, output and cost changes.
Explain the purpose and value of break-even analysis.
Distinguish gross profit, operating profit and profit for the year.
Explain the difference between profit and cash, and profit and profitability.
Assess ways of raising gross and operating profit: more revenue or lower costs.
Explain the purpose of budgeting, including zero-based budgeting.
Calculate and interpret adverse and favourable budget variances.
Explain payables and receivables and the value of cash flow forecasting.
Weigh ways to improve cash flow: debt factoring, faster customer payment, incentives, credit checks, slower supplier payment, lower outgoings.
Complete and interpret cash flow forecasts.
Calculate current ratio, acid test ratio, payables days and receivables days.
Interpret and amend the income statement and statement of financial position.
Calculate profit margins, ROCE, return on investment and gearing.
Use trends, benchmarking and context; recognise limits of financial reporting.
Assess profits, ROCE, cash flow, gearing, shareholder rewards, break-even and variances against objectives and competitors.
Explain HR objectives: numbers and skills, turnover, engagement, costs, equality, diversity, inclusion and belonging.
Explain the purpose of HR planning: recruitment, training, retention, redeployment, redundancy.
Weigh forms of employment: part-time, full-time, temporary, permanent, zero-hours, freelance, flexible.
Explain influences on HR planning, links to other functions and effect on competitiveness.
Explain the value of measuring engagement, representation, diversity, wellbeing and employee KPIs.
Calculate employee productivity, sales per employee, turnover and employee costs as a percentage of revenue.
Explain span of control and levels of hierarchy; compare tall and flat structures.
Compare centralisation and decentralisation and restructuring such as delayering.
Explain autocratic, democratic and transformational leadership and their impact on performance.
Explain the purpose of appraisal and the challenges of acquiring, developing and retaining talent.
Explain the value of teams and Hackman's model of team effectiveness.
Explain benefits and challenges of motivating staff.
Apply motivation theories of Taylor, Maslow and Herzberg.
Weigh financial rewards: wages, salaries, piece rate, commission, performance pay, shares, fringe benefits.
Weigh non-financial rewards: delegation, empowerment, job enrichment, training, remote and flexible working.
Explain benefits and challenges of improving wellbeing and methods such as health support and flexible working.
Explain employee voice and representation, including unions and forums.
Explain causes and consequences of poor relations and how to improve them.
Explain operations objectives: efficiency, quality, volume, flexibility, environmental impact.
Explain how operations add value and factors in choosing a location.
Explain links to other functions and effect on competitiveness.
Calculate employee productivity, unit costs and resource and capacity utilisation.
Interpret KPIs such as wait times, defects, complaints, delivery times and satisfaction, and environmental measures.
Explain resource utilisation and efficiency.
Weigh ways to improve efficiency: capacity use, lean production, kaizen, waste reduction, scheduling, productivity, cost control.
Explain quality and the costs of poor quality.
Weigh quality methods: quality control, assurance, TQM, quality circles, benchmarking.
Explain the value of sustainable operations and ways to cut impact.
Explain challenges: cost, supply chain limits, disruption.
Weigh ways to match supply to demand: scheduling, inventory, flexible employment, outsourcing, investment, capacity.
Explain challenges of not matching supply to demand.
Weigh producing internally versus buying in.
Explain the value of managing suppliers and logistics and influences on choosing suppliers.
Explain supply chain issues, profit distribution along the chain, transparency and accreditations.
Explain reasons for holding inventory and influences on amount held.
Compare just-in-time and just-in-case control.
Calculate and interpret inventory turnover.
Explain the value and challenges of innovation, ways to develop it and protecting it with patents and copyrights.
Explain project management and network analysis.
Interpret and amend network diagrams; calculate float and the critical path.
Explain technical, purchasing and financial economies of scale.
Explain diseconomies of scale: control, communication, coordination.
Explain the use of technology including AI in inventory, supply chain and automation to improve competitiveness.

units.title: 3.1 Unit: What is business? Managing marketing and finance

outcomes.text: Explain the purpose, value and challenges of marketing internationally and adapting the marketing mix.
Discuss ethical issues in product, promotion and pricing decisions.
Discuss ethical issues with tax avoidance and payment terms for customers and suppliers.
Explain codes of conduct and ethical issues of equality, diversity, inclusion and pay gaps.
Explain supplier codes of conduct and audits, and ethical issues in sourcing, product safety and environmental impact.
Explain the purpose of business values and factors shaping culture: leadership, mission, rewards, structure, customers.
Assess the impact of positive and negative culture and reasons for and challenges of changing it.
Explain how culture affects competitiveness.

units.title: 3.3 Unit: Business and society, the external environment, and strategy (A-level only)

outcomes.text: Explain sustainability: environmental, social and economic.
Explain challenges of implementing sustainability and the Triple Bottom Line (people, planet, profit).
Explain CSR and Carroll's pyramid.
Compare shareholder and stakeholder approaches.
Distinguish CSR from PR, including greenwashing and bluewashing.
Explain ESG reporting and its measures, such as health and safety, emissions, community investment and board composition.
Explain the value of improving ESG performance.
Explain Porter's five forces: rivalry, buyer power, supplier power, entry and substitute threats.
Analyse what drives each force, its impact, and how a business can influence or respond to it.
Analyse effects of trade agreements, protectionism, consumer and employee protection, competition policy and environmental rules, and responses.
Analyse effects of GDP growth, taxation, inflation, interest rates, exchange rates and unemployment, and responses.
Calculate the effect of exchange rate changes on export prices and import costs.
Analyse effects of demographics, consumer values and activism, and responses.
Analyse opportunities and threats of digital and disruptive technologies including AI, and responses.
Explain the value of strategy and planning and assess performance using marketing, finance, HR and operations data.
Explain how quantitative and qualitative analysis shapes decisions.
Explain the purpose of mission, vision and objectives, and of SWOT analysis.
Use stakeholder mapping: power, interest, and actions and impact of stakeholders.
Weigh Ansoff Matrix strategies: market penetration, market development, new products, diversification.
Weigh positioning strategies (low-cost versus differentiation) and changing position.
Explain factors in successful implementation: resources, planning, leadership, communication, external factors.
Explain why competitiveness is lost, including strategic drift.
Explain the value of capital investment and factors influencing it.
Calculate and interpret payback, average rate of return and net present value.
Weigh being an SME, reasons for and challenges of growth, organic versus inorganic growth.
Weigh mergers, acquisitions, franchising and vertical, horizontal and conglomerate integration.
Explain sustainable growth, retrenchment and effects on functional areas.
Weigh opportunities and threats of going global and attractiveness of markets.
Weigh entry methods: exporting, licensing, joint ventures, direct investment; and glocalisation.
Weigh producing abroad and the effect of global strategy on functions.
Explain the value of a digital strategy and its impact on functions and competitiveness.
Explain internal and external reasons for change and its effects on stakeholders.
Explain resistance to change (Kotter and Schlesinger) and managing change with Lewin's force field analysis.
Explain types of risk: financial, strategic, operational, compliance, reputational, cybersecurity.
Weigh ways to manage risk: research, forecasting, contingency plans, succession, insurance, diversification, training, cybersecurity.
Weigh ways to manage uncertainty: scenario planning and building an agile business.
